children: By Bharath Rajeswaran and Vivek Kumar M
Indian shares edged lower on Tuesday as rising crude prices and bond yields due to escalating Middle East tensions offset optimism over stronger-than-expected domestic economic growth.
The Nifty 50
fell 0.13% to 24,050.25 and the BSE Sensex
shed 0.05% to 76,923.88 as of 10:21 a.m. IST.
Nine of the 16 major sectors logged losses. Bank index
fell 1%, about 600 points, reversing the roughly 500-point gain it recorded in the closing auction session on Monday.
The broader small-caps
and mid-caps
lost 0.3% and 1.1%, respectively.
India's economy grew 7.8% year-on-year in the April-June quarter, surpassing forecasts as investment and manufacturing strengthened alongside resilient consumer demand.

However, renewed Middle East fighting lifted crude prices, raising worries about inflation and U.S. rate hikes, and pushed global bond yields higher. Oil prices rose about 1% to $91.30 a barrel, extending the previous session's 2.5% gain.

"The way yields are rising everywhere tells you the market is now firmly pricing a U.S. rate hike this year with crude continuing to spiral higher," said Shrikant Chouhan, head of equity research at Kotak Securities.

U.S. 10-year yields hit 20-month highs after hawkish Federal Reserve commentary, while German and French yields reached 15-year peaks. India's benchmark 10-year yield also neared 7%, reflecting global rate pressures that could curb foreign inflows and raise borrowing costs.
Among individual stocks, Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri
surged 20% after Chennai-based GRT Jewellers agreed to buy a controlling stake in the jewellery retailer.
Happiest Minds
fell 4.7% after ITC
said its IT unit would buy a 22.1% stake in the software services provider. ITC gained 3%.
Morgan Stanley said the deal would expand ITC Infotech's U.S. footprint and boost shareholder value.
Newly listed Milky Mist Dairy
gained 7.3% after a quarterly profit rise.
Godrej Agrovet
climbed 8.5% after Kotak reiterated "buy", citing strong growth prospects and attractive valuations.
Bharti Airtel
added 2.6% after HSBC retained "buy".
